Aaron Li: Heads-up — I'm seeing our EU region headroom model blow up when we factor in next week's marketing surge + scheduled network maintenance. Quick sanity check?
Maya Chen: can you paste the sim run? what's the assumed client concurrency and tokens/sec?
Aaron Li: Sim run: 2.5M expected tokens/sec across region peak, concurrent requests 18k, avg seq 220 tokens, p95 latency target 150ms. Using default batch=64.
Aaron Li: ```bash
./simulate_throughput --region eu --tokens_per_sec 2500000 --concurrency 18000 --avg_seq 220 --batch 64 --p95 150ms
```
infra-bot: Scheduled network maintenance in eu-west-1: 2026-03-22 03:00-04:00 UTC — potential 10-20% cross-AZ bandwidth reduction.
Chen Park: If bandwidth drops 15% our effective tokens/sec capacity per GPU drops ~12% due to KV sync stalls. Need plan: bump reserved capacity or degrade to smaller model?
Priya Nair: Cost note — adding 10 GPUs reserved is ~+$18k/month. Could instead increase prefix cache hit target from 40% -> 60% to offset ~8% capacity loss — cheaper but needs work on cache keys and invalidation.
Maya Chen: We could also change autoscaler policy: relax p99 target (eg p99 -> 300ms) to allow larger batching windows, which reduces GPU-hours by ~9% in a quick sim. tradeoffs on latency.
Aaron Li: Let's run three quick sims: (A) +10 GPUs reserved, (B) cache tuning (40->60 hit), (C) relaxed p99. I'll kick them off and share numbers in ~30m. For now ops: @infra-bot can you add temporary scaling policy to +burst +20% for the maintenance window?
infra-bot: Done — temporary scaling policy applied for eu-* from 2026-03-22T02:45:00Z to 2026-03-22T04:15:00Z, burst +25% cap. policy_id=eu-maint-burst-1965432100
Chen Park: :thumbsup: I'll prep a minimal cache key change and a hotfix for invalidation, but timeline is ~2 days. If surge is next week we need the autoscaler burst.
Priya Nair: Also check committed capacity discounts — we might be able to reassign some spare Dedicated GPUs from staging to prod temporarily (billing team ok'd short reassignments before).
Aaron Li: Great, thanks. I'll post the sim outputs and a short recommendation in #eng-infra once runs finish.
